landscape.headline: There is no scholarly consensus on whether cryptocurrency is permissible, and AAOIFI has issued no final standard on it. Three broad positions are held by serious authorities.

positions.who: Mufti Faraz Adam (Amanah Advisors); Shariah Review Bureau (Bahrain)
positions.summary: Crypto assets can satisfy the conditions of mal and are acceptable as a medium of exchange, so spot ownership is permissible subject to the ordinary prohibitions on riba, gharar and maysir.

positions.who: Dar al-Ifta al-Misriyyah (Grand Mufti Shawki Allam); Diyanet (Türkiye)
positions.summary: Dealing in Bitcoin is prohibited: the gharar is excessive, there is no recognised issuing authority standing behind the value, and the asset facilitates speculation and illicit use.

positions.who: Mufti Muhammad Taqi Usmani; International Islamic Fiqh Academy (OIC)
positions.summary: Cautious. Mufti Taqi Usmani is reported to consider trading impermissible in its current speculative form but to leave the ruling open to revision if crypto becomes tied to real economic activity. The IIFA's 2019 resolution (237) called for further research and its 2021 symposium deferred its recommendations, so the Academy has not closed the question.

positions.who: Office of Grand Ayatollah Sayyid Ali al-Sistani
positions.summary: Withholds a ruling on buying and selling virtual currencies and directs followers to the next most learned jurist. Also holds that local law regulating crypto must be respected.

positions.who: AAOIFI (as an institution)
positions.summary: Has not issued a final Shariah standard on cryptocurrency. Its Standard No. 21 quantitative screens (interest-bearing debt and securities under 30% of market cap; non-permissible income under 5% of revenue) are designed for equities and are applied to coins only by analogy.

usage_rules.label: Leverage, margin and futures
usage_rules.detail: The prohibition here is essentially universal across schools and applies regardless of which coin is involved. You cannot sell what you do not own, and a contract whose settlement depends on a future price is gharar.

usage_rules.label: Guaranteed or fixed 'earn' yield
usage_rules.detail: Any product advertising a fixed or guaranteed return on a deposit is the definition of riba al-fadl / riba al-nasi'ah, whatever the asset it is denominated in.

usage_rules.label: Day-trading on noise with no productive intent
usage_rules.detail: Repeated short-horizon speculation is treated by many scholars as closer to gambling than investing, even when the underlying asset is permissible. Intent and holding period matter.

standards.note: AAOIFI has not issued a final Shariah standard on cryptocurrency. Its Shari'a Standard No. 21 quantitative screens were written for equities, and any application to tokens is an analogy rather than a standard.
